* *
 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by her in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
(SCCH3) 3 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 On 14.02.2023 at about 03.45 p.m, the petitioner was crossing the Amrutha College Road, Opp. C.M. Muniyallappa Complex, Chodsandra Circle, Bengaluru, at that time one Motor Cycle bearing No. KA51HQ3895 came at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.

Due to this the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately she was shifted to Sun Clinic, wherein after first aid she was admitted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and undergone operation and prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged 52 years and was doing Coolie work and was earning Rs.18,000/ p.m.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of offending Motor Cycle rider and in this regard the Bellanduru Traffic Police have registered a case against the rider of the said offending Motor Cycle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the R.C. Owner of the said offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% with costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and contended that the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and hence there was contravened the proviso of M.V. Act and terms and conditions of the policy and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Motor Cycle bearing No. KA51HQ3895 and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

The petition is bad for nonjoinder of proper and necessary parties and has further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, occupation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and contended that alleged accident is not occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motor Cycle bearing No. KA51HQ3895 and it is the negligence on the part of petitioner who was crossing road without noticing on coming vehicles and was crossing the road carelessly and caused accident.

It is contended that the insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of Anjula vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68254637/
2

5 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.

05. The respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and also denied the age, income, occupation of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and manner of accident and contended that there was a negligent on the part of petitioner.

Hence, the claim petition is devoid of bonafides and the petitioner is not entitled to claim compensation from this respondent and submits that as on the date of accident the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA51HQ3895 was having valid driving licence to ride the motor bike and was having its insurance policy bearing No.3397/02377 707/000/00 which was also valid and effective from 17.04.2021 to 16.04.2026.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner if any and pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent.

06. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues: (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 ISSUES 01. Whether the petitioner proves that the she had sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 14.02.2023 at about 03.45 p.m, on opposite C.M. Muniyallappa Complex, Amrutha College Road, Choodasandra Circle, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of riding of the Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA51HQ3895 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If, so, to what amount and from whom?

03 . What Order or Award?
e 07.

The petitioner in order to prove her case, she herself examined as PW.1 and a doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed disability and a eyewitness are got examined as PW.2 and 3 and through them 14 documents are marked as Ex.P.1 to 14 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
However, the respondents have not lead their evidence.
Hence, respondents evidence is taken as nil.
08. The learned counsel for the petitioner has filed written arguments and I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the respondents and perused the records.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3

sentences.text: 3  REASONS 10. Issue No.1: The petitioner in order to prove her case, she herself examined as PW.1 and in her chiefexamination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.

During the course of cross examination by the counsel for respondent No.1 she has stated that on the date of accident she was crossing the road from right side towards left side near Amrutha College and admits that at the place of crossing the road there is no signal and denied to the suggestion that this accident occurred due to her negligence and not due to the negligence of offending Motor Cycle and further stated that her son had lodged complaint to the Police after 3 days of accident as her son was looking after her and denied to the suggestion that she has sustained injuries due to some other vehicle and in order to claim compensation, after 04 (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 days false complaint was lodged against the offending Motor Cycle and denied to the suggestion that she had not obtained followup treatment and implants are removed and wounds are healedup and denied to the suggestion that she has not spent Rs.75,000/ towards her medical and other expenses and free treatment was given at Sanjay Gandhi hospital and denied to the suggestion that she was aged about more than 60 years and she was not doing Coolie work and not earning Rs.18,000/ p.m.
11.

Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained right leg both bone mid 1/3rd shaft fracture and he assessed particular limb disability at 42% and whole body disability at 14% and has produced Outpatient record, Case sheet and Xrays as per Ex.P.12 to 14.

During the course of cross examination by the respondent No.1 counsel he stated that he has treated the petitioner along with his unit and admits that he has not conducted any surgery to the petitioner and as per records one Dr.Aniruddh has conducted surgery and after discharging from the hospital petitioner has took followup treatment from him and admits that petitioner has got BPL card and there was a (SCCH 3) 9 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 concession in the medical treatment who hold BPL card and Rs.29,000/
has sanctioned as concession amount and that bill amount was Rs.17,250/ and after concession amount was sanctioned, deposit amount has been returned back to the petitioner and admits that fractures are united and implants are not removed and admits that there is no fracture on knee and ankle and there was a implants in knee and ankle and denied to the suggestion that only after removal of implants in knee and ankle, disability can be assessed and also denied to the suggestion that after removal of implants, mobility component and stability component may reduce and he has not advised any treatment to improve restrictions and admits that he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability and also stated that since petitioner was obtained the Ayushmanbhav Health facility, hence there is no need to future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/,
for that witness voluntaries it all depends on hospital authorities and denied to the suggestion that though there is no difficulties and disability, in order to help the petitioner, he has falsely assessed the disability.

12. Further, the PW.3 who is said to be eyewitness to the accident has also stated about rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Motor (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 Cycle and Anjula vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68254637/
4 caused injuries to the petitioner and in the crossexamination by the respondent No.1 counsel he stated that there is no signal and zebra crossing in the accident spot and one Honda Shine Motor Cycle was caused accident.

sentences.text: 13. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14 on her behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Bellanduru Traffic Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against rider of the offending Motor Cycle for his rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle who caused the accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of IMV report which discloses that the involvement of the offending Motor Cycle in the alleged accident.
Ex. P.5 is copy of Wound certificate which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against rider of offending Motor Cycle and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Motor Cycle and caused grievous injuries to the petitioner.

Ex.P.7 is Discharge (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 summary of Sanjay Gandhi hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein she was treated as inpatient from 14.02.2023 to 24.02.2023 for 10 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.8 and 12 are outpatient records.
Ex.P.13 is Case sheet and Ex.P.14 is X rays.

14. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioner, which clearly establishes that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 14.02.2023 at about 03.45 p.m, on opposite to C.M. Muniyallappa Complex,
Amrutha College Road, Chodsandra Circle, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing No. KA51HQ3895, by its rider as alleged in the petition.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved the Issue No.1.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.
The petitioner in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident she was aged about 52 years and was doing Coolie work and was earning Rs.18,000/ p.m.

Due to the accidental (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 injuries she became permanent disablement and suffered pain and sufferings,
unable to do work.
16. It is duty of the petitioner to prove her age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show her exact date of birth.
However, she has produced Ex.P.9 Aadhaar card wherein her birth year is mentioned as 1971 and the alleged accident occurred on 14.02.2023.
Hence, eventhough this document is taken into consideration, it appears that as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 52 years.

Hence, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 52 years and as per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 is 11.

sentences.text: With regard to her avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding her avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the LokAdalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/ p.m.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/.
18.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained right leg both bone mid 1/3rd shaft fracture and he assessed particular limb disability at 42% and whole body disability at 14%.

Hence, considering the evidence of PW.2 and grievous injuries sustained and medical records,
this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 14%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 Discharge summary, according to which she was admitted in the hospital as inpatient for total period of 10 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 food and conveyance charges, she is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.
20. Pain and sufferings:

As per Ex.P.5 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and Ex.P.8 Outpatient records, Ex.P.12 Outpatient record, Ex.P.13 is Case sheet and Ex.P.14 is Xrays and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained right leg both bone mid 1/3rd shaft fracture.
Accordingly with regard to fracture suffered by her in the accident, she is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.
21. Loss of income during laid up period:

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,000/ p.m and she has admitted in the hospital for 10 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of her stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for atleast 02 months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/
(Rs.16,000 x 2) under this head.
Medical expenses:
As per Ex.P.10 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.8,147/.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,147/ under this head.
23. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in her future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/

sentences.text: 24. Future medical expenses:

According to doctor PW.2 the petitioner has difficulty in doing daily routine activities and she needs one more surgery in the form of implant removal for which approximate cost of Rs.25,000/ is required.

Hence, under the facts and circumstances of the case,
under this head the petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/.
25.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
1.
Loss of future income 2,95,68000 2. Pain and Sufferings 30,00000 (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 3.
Attendant charges, extra 30,00000 nutritious food and conveyance charges 4.
Medical Expenses 8,14700 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,00000 unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 32,00000 period 7.
Future medical expenses 25,00000 Total 4,50,82700 26.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,50,827/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/) from the date of petition till its realization.
27. The respondents have taken contention that there is delay of 4 days in lodging the complaint and it creates doubt about the alleged accident and injury sustained by the petitioner.

In this regard the counsel for the petitioner relied upon the Judgment reported in 2011 ACJ 911 in between Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court is held that, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
section 166(1) - Claim application - FIR - Delay in lodging - Effect of - Truck while being reversed hit and injured a minor boy (SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 sitting on the side of the road in front of his house - Accident was witnessed by father of injured and another person and they took him to hospital -
Cause of injury mentioned in injury report prepared by the doctor in road accident -
Police came to hospital on the next day of accident but no FIR was recorded as father of injured was under mental agony and stress and he was more concerned to get medical treatment for his son -

Father lodged FIR after 3 months of accident and he explained the reasons that his son was seriously injured and his treatment was more important; some persons in the locality pressurized him that compensation matter could be sorted out amicably since driver of vehicle was his neighbour; and he was not aware of the niceties of law that lodging of FIR was condition precedent for filing claim application - Owner of truck admitted the accident -

Neither the driver entered witness box to deny the accident nor the opposite parties led any evidence in rebutted to the evidence of the claimant - Anjula vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68254637/

sentences.text: 7 Occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent driving of truck by its driver is thus established
- Tribunal dismissed claim application on the ground that FIR was lodged belatedly - High Court upheld the order of the tribunal -
Whether the claim application can be dismissed on (SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 the ground of delay in lodging FIR
- Held: no; lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting claim application (paras 18, 20, 21, 22).

The said decision is aptly applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case on hand,
since neither the Motor Cycle rider entered into witness box to deny the accident nor examined any witnesses to rebut the evidence of the claimant by the respondents, the occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent manner riding of offending Motor Cycle by its rider is established.
28.

Further, the respondent No.1 in para 6 of written statement and respondent No.2 in para 9 of his written statement admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending Motor Cycle bearing No. KA51HQ3895 in favour of respondent No.2 is valid from 17.04.2021 to 16.04.2026.
The alleged accident was occurred on 14.02.2023.
Hence, as on the date of accident the insurance policy is valid and is in force.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the R.C. Owner of the offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as (SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 on the date of accident, respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount with interest from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,50,827/ (Rupees Four lakhs fifty thousand eight hundred and twenty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 75% of the award amount through Epayment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 25% shall be kept in fixed (SCCH3) 20 M.V.C.No.2241/2023 deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
